instantiated_cells.justification: State agencies file a separate statement under §13.695 identifying officers/employees who lobby and are exempted from the standard lobbyist registration/licensing regime (§§13.63, 13.64, 13.65, 13.68) by §13.621(2).

The Governor is an elective state official; §13.621(3) exempts elective state officials acting in official capacity from §§13.63, 13.64, 13.65, 13.68, and 13.695, and §13.62(8) treats the Governor's action on bills/proposals as legislative action itself, not lobbying requiring registration.
Independent agencies fall within the §13.62(2) definition of "agency" and therefore file under §13.695 rather than registering as principals/lobbyists, per the §13.621(2) exemption.

Section 13.621(1)(d) makes the entire subchapter inapplicable to "Lobbying of an agency official by an agency official of a different agency or another agency official of the same agency," so no registration is required.

Section 13.621(3) exempts legislative employees acting in official capacity from §§13.63, 13.64, 13.65, 13.68, and 13.695, and §13.62(2) excludes legislative councils/committees from the definition of "agency."

A lobbying firm that employs lobbyists falls within the §13.62(12) definition of "principal" ("any person who employs a lobbyist") and must register under §13.64 when expenditures exceed $500; its individual lobbyists must also be licensed under §13.63.

Section 13.625(4m)(e) and (f) expressly contemplate "a principal that is a local governmental unit," confirming that local governments employing lobbyists are principals subject to registration under §13.64; they are not within the §13.621(2) state-agency exemption (which applies only to §13.62(2) "agencies").

Section 13.63(1)(a) requires lobbyists to obtain a license from the commission, and §13.66 prohibits any person from engaging in lobbying as a lobbyist unless licensed under §13.63 and authorized under §13.65.

Section 13.64(1) requires "Every principal who makes expenditures or incurs obligations in an aggregate amount exceeding $500 in a calendar year for the purpose of engaging in lobbying" to file a registration statement with the commission.

"Principal" under §13.62(12) is "any person who employs a lobbyist" without exclusion for non-agency public entities; such entities employing lobbyists must register under §13.64 if expenditures exceed $500, since only §13.62(2) "agencies" qualify for the §13.621(2) state-agency exemption.

Section 13.62(11) defines "lobbyist" as one employed by a principal or who "contracts for or receives economic consideration, other than reimbursement for actual expenses, from a principal"; an unpaid volunteer receiving no economic consideration is not a lobbyist and need not be licensed, and §13.621(6) further protects individuals lobbying solely on their own behalf.

content.text:
I'll analyze each entity type against the Wisconsin lobbying statute to determine registration requirements.

Key statute references:
- §13.64: Principals (those who employ lobbyists) with expenditures >$500 must register
- §13.63: Lobbyists must be licensed
- §13.695: State agencies file separate statements (not standard lobbyist registration)
- §13.621(1)(d): Agency-to-agency lobbying exempt
- §13.621(3): Elective state officials, local officials, tribal officials, legislative employees acting in official capacity exempt
- §13.62(2): "Agency" excludes legislative councils/committees
- §13.62(12): Principal = any person who employs a lobbyist
